biodiversity_overview.text: 22,955 GBIF occurrence records for 69 tracked species are attributed to Goa, spanning 1951-2026.
20,825 of these records (90.7%) are located to within 10 km.

species_richness.text: Observed tracked species by group: Aves 26, Magnoliopsida 15, Mammalia 11, Squamata 5, Amphibia 4, Testudines 3, Actinopterygii 3, Crocodylia 1, Elasmobranchii 1.

threatened_species.text: 8 species with records here are officially threatened (IUCN CR/EN/VU). Names and categories from the IUCN Red List export are not shown in this public snapshot.
1 further species are threatened according to the project's unverified reference list: Mugger Crocodile (VU).

notable_species.text: Most recorded species: Indian Golden Oriole (3,079), Indian Paradise-flycatcher (2,658), Indian Cormorant (2,040), Indian Pitta (1,910), Indian Scimitar-Babbler (1,694).

temporal_trends.text: Records per year went from 1,541 in 2016 to 279 in 2025. This reflects recording effort as much as wildlife and is not a population trend.

protection_coverage.text: Wildlife protected areas (OpenStreetMap national parks, sanctuaries and reserves) cover 21.1% of Goa's area (13 areas intersect the state).
20.4% of precisely located records fall inside these areas (4,253 of 20,825); this is not a measure of habitat protection.

risk_indicators.text: Highest model-predicted vulnerability among species recorded here (MODEL PREDICTION, not IUCN status): Indian Courser (0.47), Mugger Crocodile (0.46), Green Turtle (0.40), Indian Ash Tree (0.36), Indian Gooseberry (0.35).

conservation_priority.text: Top experimental CIPI grid cells in Goa (equal-weight reference): cell near 15.375N 73.875E (overall rank 63, median rank across weightings 74); cell near 14.625N 73.875E (overall rank 163, median rank across weightings 169).

environmental_pressures.text: Tree cover of at least 30% canopy covered 1,415 km2 (39.39% of land) in 2000 (Hansen Global Forest Change; includes plantations).

10.3 km2 of that tree cover was lost in 2001-2024 (0.73% of the 2000 extent; 0.37% in 2015-2024, rank 20 of 35 states). The largest annual loss was in 2011 (1.16 km2). Loss includes plantation harvest and natural disturbance; regrowth is not subtracted.
Built-up surfaces cover 1.31% of land and population density is 432.0 people per km2 (GHSL 2020).
29% of 30 m tree-cover pixels lie on a forest edge (a fragmentation indicator; higher means more fragmented).
These describe pressures on places; they do not show effects on any species.

sources: Hansen et al. Global Forest Change 2000-2024 v1.12 (CC BY 4.0)
GHSL R2023A built-up and population 2020 (CC BY 4.0)
